recipes.yield: 4 servings; one thigh and one-quarter of carrots each
recipes.time: 15 minutes prep + 25-35 minutes roasting + 3 minutes rest
ingredients: 4 boneless skinless chicken thighs, about 1 pound (454 g) total
4 medium carrots (about 300 g), cut into 1/4-inch diagonal slices
1 small orange, washed; use 1 teaspoon zest and 2 tablespoons juice
instructions: Heat the oven to 425 F (218 C). Check the chicken label for added solution or phosphates; keep the thighs refrigerated while preparing produce.
Wash carrots, orange and rosemary under running water. Slice carrots, grate the orange zest and squeeze the measured juice on a clean produce surface.
Mix the olive oil, orange zest, juice, rosemary, garlic and pepper in a bowl.
Toss the carrots with half the mixture and spread them on a rimmed baking sheet.
On a separate raw-poultry surface, pat the skinless thighs dry and coat with the remaining mixture. Wash hands and clean utensils after raw-poultry contact.
Set the thighs among the carrots with space between pieces; roast for 15 minutes.
Turn the carrots with a utensil reserved for this cooking stage and roast for another 10-20 minutes, until carrots are tender.
Check the thickest part of each thigh reaches at least 165 F (74 C) with a clean thermometer; extend cooking as needed.
Rest briefly, then use clean serving utensils to plate one thigh and one-quarter of the carrots per person.
Refrigerate leftovers promptly in shallow containers; follow the storage note.

Citrus is used for flavor; no sodium or potassium level is calculated. Not clinically reviewed; no universal kidney-safe claim or calculated nutrient values. Agree portions and ingredient choices with your renal dietitian. Do not substitute potassium-containing salt.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in shallow containers within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90 F (32 C), at 40 F (4 C) or below. Use within 3-4 days; reheat hot dishes to 165 F (74 C).

recipes.yield: 4 servings; one filled zucchini half each
recipes.time: 20 minutes prep + 25-30 minutes cooking and baking
ingredients: 2 medium-large zucchini, about 10 ounces (280 g) each
instructions: Heat the oven to 400 F (204 C). Check turkey and corn labels for added salt, seasoning and additives.
Wash zucchini, pepper and onion. Halve zucchini lengthwise and scoop out a shallow channel with a spoon, leaving a sturdy 1/4-inch wall.
Finely chop the scooped zucchini flesh. Put the four shells cut-side up in a baking dish with the measured water around them.
Bake the empty shells for 10 minutes while preparing the filling.
Warm oil in a skillet over medium heat; cook onion and pepper for 4 minutes, then add turkey using a dedicated raw-poultry utensil.
Break turkey into crumbles and cook for 6-8 minutes; stir in chopped zucchini flesh, corn, oregano, paprika and pepper.
Cook until vegetables soften and turkey reaches 165 F (74 C) in several places; clean the thermometer between checks.
Divide filling evenly among the four warm zucchini shells, then bake for 10-15 minutes more, until zucchini is tender and the filling centers reach 165 F (74 C).
Let stand for 3 minutes, then serve one filled zucchini half per diner.
Chill leftovers promptly in shallow containers; follow the storage note.

recipes.dish: Cumin-Lime Tilapia with Warm Cabbage Ribbons
recipes.story_source: NorthStar original weeknight recipe; source-linked food-safety and individualized nutrition context

recipes.yield: 4 servings; one fillet and one-quarter of cabbage each
ingredients: 1 pound (454 g) tilapia, divided into four fillets and thawed in the refrigerator if frozen
4 cups (about 280 g) thinly sliced green cabbage
1 lime, washed; use 1 teaspoon zest and 1 tablespoon juice
instructions: Read the fish label for added salt or phosphate ingredients. Set out a rimmed baking sheet, skillet and food thermometer; heat the oven to 400 F (204 C).
Wash cabbage, lime and cilantro under running water. Slice cabbage and prepare zest, juice and cilantro on a clean produce board.
Warm half the oil in a skillet over medium heat; add cabbage and stir for 2 minutes.
Add water, cover and cook for 5-7 minutes until cabbage softens but retains texture; stir once or twice.
Meanwhile place chilled tilapia on the baking sheet using a separate raw-fish surface and utensil; wash hands after handling.
Rub fillets with the remaining oil, cumin and pepper; bake for 12-16 minutes, adjusting for thickness.
Check every fillet reaches 145 F (63 C) at the thickest part with a clean thermometer; cook longer if needed.
Toss warm cabbage with lime juice and half the zest and cilantro.
Divide cabbage among four plates and top each with one fillet; scatter the remaining zest and cilantro over the fish.
Refrigerate leftovers promptly in shallow containers; follow the storage note.

recipes.yield: 4 servings; one-quarter of noodles and shrimp each
ingredients: 12 ounces (340 g) raw shrimp, peeled, deveined and tails removed, thawed in the refrigerator if frozen
6 ounces (170 g) dry thin rice noodles
1 lemon, washed; use 1 tablespoon juice and 1 teaspoon zest
instructions: Check shrimp labels for salt, phosphate ingredients and sulfite preservatives; check noodles for allergens. Keep shrimp cold while preparing the other ingredients.
Wash lemon and parsley; grate zest, measure juice, chop parsley and mince peeled garlic with clean utensils.
Prepare rice noodles according to their package directions without added salt; drain and set aside briefly.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat; add garlic and stir for 30 seconds without browning.
Add shrimp in a single layer using a dedicated utensil. Cook for about 2 minutes on the first side, then turn.
Add the measured water and cook another 1-3 minutes, until all shrimp flesh is pearly white and opaque throughout; larger shrimp may need longer.
Cut a large shrimp to check that no translucent center remains. If any shrimp are underdone, continue cooking before adding noodles.
Toss drained noodles into the hot skillet with lemon juice, zest, parsley and pepper until evenly combined and steaming.
Divide into four equal portions with shrimp distributed evenly; serve promptly using clean utensils.
Refrigerate leftovers promptly in shallow containers; follow the storage note.

recipes.time: 15 minutes prep + 16-20 minutes cooking; cooked rice required
ingredients: 2 cups cooked white rice, previously chilled promptly and kept refrigerated
1 tablespoon olive oil, divided between batches
instructions: Use rice that was refrigerated promptly after cooking and is within its safe storage period; discard rice whose time or temperature history is uncertain. Read egg and flour labels.
Wash carrot and scallions under running water, then grate or slice them on a clean board.
Break up the cold rice in a mixing bowl with a fork.
Whisk pasteurized eggs in a second bowl, then combine with rice, carrot, scallions, flour and pepper. Do not taste the raw mixture.
Divide into eight equal mounds; flatten each into a pancake about 3 inches across and no more than 1/2 inch thick.
Heat half the oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat and add four pancakes without crowding.
Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, turning carefully, until both sides are golden and the centers reach 165 F (74 C) because the mixture reheats cooked rice.
Transfer to a clean plate and repeat with the remaining oil and pancakes; verify their center temperatures too.
Serve two pancakes per person while hot; do not add an unlisted sauce without checking its ingredients separately.
Chill any leftovers promptly and follow the storage note; reheat thoroughly rather than repeatedly warming and cooling.

recipes.dish: Roasted Cabbage Wedges with Mustard-Herb Yogurt

recipes.yield: 4 side servings; one wedge and one-quarter of sauce each
ingredients: 1 small green cabbage, about 1 pound (454 g), outer damaged leaves removed
instructions: Heat the oven to 425 F (218 C). Read yogurt and mustard labels, including their sodium and allergen information.
Wash cabbage and parsley under running water. Cut cabbage through the core into four equal wedges, keeping enough core attached to hold each wedge together.
Place wedges on a rimmed baking sheet and brush their cut faces with olive oil.
Season with black pepper and arrange with one cut face down.
Roast for 15 minutes, then turn carefully with a spatula.
Roast for another 15-20 minutes until edges brown and the core is tender when pierced; reduce heat slightly if leaves darken too quickly.
While cabbage cooks, combine pasteurized yogurt, mustard, parsley and vinegar in a clean bowl.
Cover the sauce and keep it refrigerated at 40 F (4 C) or below until serving.
Place one hot wedge on each of four plates; spoon one-quarter of the cold yogurt sauce alongside each wedge.
Refrigerate leftover cabbage and sauce promptly in separate shallow containers; follow the storage note.

recipes.time: 20 minutes prep + 12 minutes filling + 15 minutes cooling + 20-25 minutes baking; pastry thawing additional
ingredients: 1 sheet frozen puff pastry (about 8-9 ounces / 227-255 g), thawed in the refrigerator according to the package
instructions: Thaw pastry in the refrigerator according to its label and keep it cold until shaping. Read pastry ingredients for wheat, milk, egg, soy and sodium.
Wash mushrooms, onion and rosemary under running water, dry mushrooms, then chop produce finely.
Warm olive oil in a skillet over medium heat; cook onion for 4 minutes.
Add mushrooms, rosemary and pepper; cook for 7-8 minutes, stirring until the mushrooms soften and released moisture mostly evaporates.
Spread filling in a shallow clean dish and cool for about 15 minutes until no longer hot; do not leave it out beyond safe time limits. Heat the oven to 400 F (204 C).
Dust a board with the measured flour, unfold the chilled pastry and roll gently into roughly a 10-inch square; cut into four equal squares.
Divide cooled filling among the squares, keeping it on one half and leaving a clear 1/2-inch edge.
Moisten edges sparingly with water, fold each square into a triangle, press firmly and crimp with a fork; cut a small steam vent in each top.
Bake on a parchment-lined tray for 20-25 minutes or until the package-directed bake is complete, pastry is golden and layers are cooked through; do not taste uncooked pastry.
Cool for 5 minutes before serving one pie per person; refrigerate leftovers promptly and follow the storage note.

Add vanilla, lime juice and optional sugar to the pineapple; stir for 30 seconds.
Fluff couscous with a fork and fold in the warm pineapple mixture.
Divide evenly among four small cups or bowls and serve warm.

ingredients: 6 slices white sandwich bread (about 180 g), cut into 1-inch cubes
1 cup (about 150 g) peeled peach slices, fresh or plain frozen and thawed in the refrigerator
1 teaspoon olive oil for the dish
instructions: Heat the oven to 350 F (177 C). Read bread, milk and egg labels, and oil an 8-inch-square baking dish with the measured oil.
If using fresh peaches, wash them under running water before peeling, pitting and slicing; keep thawed frozen peaches refrigerated until assembling.
Cut bread into one-inch cubes on a clean board and place half in the baking dish.
Scatter half the peaches over the bread, then add the remaining bread and peaches.
Whisk pasteurized eggs with pasteurized milk, sugar, cinnamon and vanilla in a clean bowl.
Pour the mixture evenly over the bread; press gently so all pieces moisten and let stand for 10 minutes. Do not taste raw egg mixture.
Bake for 30 minutes, then check the center; cover loosely with foil if the top browns before the middle sets.
Continue baking as needed, usually up to 10 minutes more, until the center reaches 165 F (74 C) with a clean thermometer and no liquid custard remains.
Rest for 10 minutes before cutting into four equal portions; serve one portion per person.
Refrigerate leftovers promptly in shallow containers and follow the storage note.

recipes.yield: 6 servings; two cookies each from twelve
recipes.time: 15 minutes prep + 30 minutes chilling + 18-22 minutes baking + 15 minutes cooling
ingredients: 1/4 cup (57 g) unsalted butter made from pasteurized milk, softened
instructions: Read flour, butter and vanilla labels for allergens. Wash the lemon under running water before grating the measured zest.
Beat softened butter and sugar together in a clean bowl until creamy, about 2 minutes.
Mix in vanilla and lemon zest until evenly distributed.
Add flour and stir just until crumbly, then gently press into a cohesive dough; do not taste raw flour or dough.
Shape into a log about 4 inches long and 1 1/2 inches in diameter; wrap and refrigerate for 30 minutes until firm.
Heat the oven to 325 F (163 C) and line a baking sheet with baking parchment.
Cut the chilled log into twelve equal rounds, about 1/3 inch thick; arrange on the sheet with at least 1 inch between cookies.
Bake for 18-22 minutes until the edges are light gold and the surfaces are set; avoid browning them deeply.
Cool on the sheet for 5 minutes, then transfer carefully to a rack for another 10 minutes. Serve two cookies per portion.
Once fully cool, cover the extra cookies; for a conservative home-storage plan refrigerate and use within 3-4 days, or freeze in a labeled airtight container.
